boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Little Blue River record (October 21, 1864) in Price's Missouri Expedition [September-October 1864]. The October 20 withdrawal to Independence and the evening fighting in the streets of Independence on the 21st are context; the October 22 action at Independence is a separate record (MO025). Campaign-wide marches, recruiting, destruction, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 1st Division, Army of the Border and Army of Missouri; the live field reads zero. NPS gives Blunt's force as about 2,000 and says Confederate numerical superiority told in the five-hour fight. Britton says Moonlight's Second Brigade held the crossing and Blunt brought Jennison's and Ford's brigades and McLain's battery of five 3-inch rifles, with Marmaduke, Shelby and then Fagan crossing. Price says Lawther's regiment met the enemy in superior numbers, Greene came up with about 150 men, and his troops held against far superior numbers.
claims.rationale: Unit identifications and contradictory statements of numerical superiority; no count at the action. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

open_questions: Curtis's (No. 64), Blunt's (No. 80), Moonlight's (No. 82), Ford's (No. 84), Clark's and Greene's reports remain deferred.

Rosecrans's, Pleasonton's and Curtis's reports, the subordinate Union and Confederate reports in Volume XLI Part 1, the organization of Price's army (No. 89), Maclean's itinerary (No. 90), the Price Court of Inquiry, Hinton's 1865 Rebel Invasion of Missouri and Kansas, maps and returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family (the NPS battle page plus the frozen Arnold rows). Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, volume II (Putnam, 1899) is a retrospective history by a Union participant; by its preface the larger operations are based mainly on the published official reports, so it is not independent of the Price report family. Price's September 19 and November 2 dispatches and his December 28, 1864 report (Official Records Series I, Volume XLI, Part 1, No. 88) are one family of interested Confederate accounts. The Official Records volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
